lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Check that the code link leads directly to relevant, maintained work.
items.because: A reviewer should be able to inspect the work quickly.

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are unnecessary for a U.S.-style résumé, do not establish technical fit, and may invite bias.

items.says: The opening lacks a brief target-role descriptor or summary.
items.because: It does not immediately establish whether the target is ML engineering, agent engineering, or general software.

items.says: Make the in-progress master’s degree unmistakable at a glance.
items.because: The degree is not yet completed.

items.says: Make the education location detail consistent, particularly “Country.”
items.because: The two institutions use different levels of location detail.

items.says: Consider placing experience before education.
items.because: Relevant work experience may deserve earlier placement for industry ML engineering roles.

items.says: Define and substantiate the 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement.
items.because: Its calculation, evaluation set, and baseline are unclear, making the result hard to assess.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and over what sample.
items.because: The 14%-to-6% metric is not self-explanatory.

items.says: Clarify the relationship between the specialist agents and independent reviewer.
Clarify the equal-accuracy comparison and how the reductions were measured.
items.because: The experiment and baseline need to be clear.

items.says: Make the main GRPO result easier to extract quickly.
items.because: The bullet is technically strong but dense.

items.says: Say whether the evaluation harness entered the release process or served a one-time comparison.
items.because: A reader needs to understand how the team used it.

items.says: Explain what the harness evaluated and how it detected the regressions.
items.because: The two caught regressions need more context.

items.says: The assistant-only loss-masking contribution repeats the first internship bullet.
items.because: As written, it uses space without adding much evidence.

items.says: Consider moving the triage-branch result higher in the internship.
items.because: It appears last despite a strong operational impact metric.

items.says: Reduce and prioritize the six internship bullets.
items.because: Six is a lot for an internship, especially with repeated subject matter.

items.says: Give workload or infrastructure context for the 4x GPU-memory reduction.
items.because: The reader cannot tell why the change mattered.

items.says: Indicate whether the load tests represented production-like load, if space allows.
“Adds” switches to present tense within a past-tense role.
items.because: The inconsistency could suggest insufficient review.

items.says: Specify what the automated regression checks covered.
Explain how the three-day release-cycle figure was measured.
Quantify the nightly backlogs or their effect on dispatch.
items.because: The outcome is less measurable than the migration itself.

items.says: Consider leading the Junior Software Engineer entry with the most role-relevant achievements.
items.because: Latency and fleet migration may be more immediately legible than the precision and memory detail.

items.says: Replace or substantiate the “AI-first engineering practices” bullet.
items.because: Its adoption and impact claims show no specific change or measurable result.

items.says: Define the stress-test setup and what 100x raw-conversation growth means.
items.because: The scale of the test is difficult to interpret.

items.says: State what behavior or quality survived the context reduction.
items.because: Token reduction alone does not establish system quality.

items.says: Give the workload, failure conditions, and validation context for the concurrency fix.
items.because: “50-way fan-out” alone does not show when or how often failures occurred.

items.says: Make your personal scope clearer than “Contributor.”
items.because: The role label is broad.

items.says: Identify the open-source framework clearly enough to verify the contribution.
items.because: The project is not named specifically.

items.says: Explain how the injected-degradation trials were designed.
Explain what the 0.89 Kendall correlation demonstrates.
items.because: Readers must otherwise infer whether it shows sensitivity, ranking agreement, or something else.

items.says: The triage-backlog result duplicates the internship achievement.
items.because: Presenting the same outcome as a separate project achievement risks looking like double-counting.

items.says: The skills list is thin relative to the experience described.
items.because: It may undersell relevant ML and agent engineering capabilities.

items.says: Replace or supplement the broad term “agent evaluation” with specific methods or tools.
items.because: The projects describe more specific citation, faithfulness, and correlation-based evaluation work.

items.says: No explicit cloud/platform, model-serving, or deployment-stack experience is listed.
items.because: That may be a serious gap depending on the target job.
